title: Responsive Design and Media Queries
description: Understanding how to make websites adapt to different screen sizes using media queries and responsive design principles.

quiz.question: What is the main goal of responsive web design?
options: Make websites look good on all devices
quiz.correctAnswer: Make websites look good on all devices
quiz.explanation: Responsive design ensures websites adapt to different screen sizes and devices.

quiz.question: Which CSS feature is primarily used to apply styles based on device characteristics?
quiz.explanation: Media queries allow CSS to be applied conditionally based on screen size, resolution, etc.

quiz.question: How do you write a media query for devices with a maximum width of 600px?
quiz.explanation: Correct syntax uses parentheses and max-width in media queries.

quiz.question: Which unit is commonly used in responsive design to represent a percentage of the viewport width?
quiz.explanation: vw (viewport width) units are relative to the width of the viewport.

quiz.question: What does the 'viewport' meta tag in HTML do?
quiz.explanation: The viewport meta tag tells browsers how to adjust page dimensions on mobile.

quiz.question: Which media query targets devices with a minimum screen width of 768px?
quiz.explanation: min-width targets devices equal or wider than the specified width.

quiz.question: Which CSS property is often used alongside media queries to create flexible layouts?
quiz.explanation: Flexbox provides a flexible layout structure that works well with responsive design.

quiz.question: True or False: Responsive design always requires multiple versions of the same HTML page.
quiz.explanation: Responsive design uses one HTML page with CSS to adapt layout, no need for multiple pages.

quiz.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the font size of the root element?
quiz.explanation: rem units are relative to the root element’s font size, useful in responsive typography.

quiz.question: What is the effect of using 'display: none;' inside a media query?
options: Hides an element on certain screen sizes
Deletes an element from the DOM
Makes element visible on all devices
quiz.correctAnswer: Hides an element on certain screen sizes
quiz.explanation: 'display: none;' hides the element but it still exists in the DOM.
